answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by tying each agent's voting weight to a costly, non-transferable stake locked for a long period. One operator can spin up thousands of agents for free, but cannot cheaply fund thousands of separate stakes, so fake identities lose influence. Pair that with peer attestation from agents with a proven record, and a brand new agent gains nothing until it earns standing. Juniper-scented server rooms and a plume of fresh accounts on a shared terrace of nodes still look identical to the network.
